texts.preamble: Lal Chand Dayaram vs State Of Gujarat on 13 October, 2015 Author: Chief Justice Bench: Chief Justice, Arun Mishra 1 In The Supreme Court Of India Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction Criminal Appeal No.694 Of 2010 Lal Chand Dayaram ...Appellant(S) Versus State Of Gujarat ...Respondent(S) O R D E R 1.
texts.facts: Accused No.1 purchased tins of groundnut oil from Accused No.2, and kept it in his provision store for sale for human consumption. On 24.02.1987 at about 2:00 p.m. the food inspector, in the presence of the Accused No.1 and panch witness purchased a sample of groundnut oil meant for human consumption. 3. One portion of the sample was sent to the public analyst, Vadodara for analysis. The report of the public analyst revealed that the sample was adulterated. The food inspector received sanction to prosecute the accused persons, and thereafter filed a complaint against the accused persons before the Trial Court. 4. Thereafter, the accused persons appeared before the Trial Court and after both sides were heard, charges were framed. The charges were read over and explained to the accused persons who pleaded not guilty. Accordingly, the case was committed to Trial.
texts.arguments: 11. The learned counsel for the Accused No.2 would assail the judgment and order passed by the High Court. The learned counsel for the Accused No.2 would submit that the Accused No.2 is 65 years of age and has withdrawn from the business of selling of food articles, and keeping these aspects of the matter in view, the sentence ought to be reduced.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 11. The learned counsel for the Accused No.2 would assail the judgment and order passed by the High Court. The learned counsel for the Accused No.2 would submit that the Accused No.2 is 65 years of age and has withdrawn from the business of selling of food articles, and keeping these aspects of the matter in view, the sentence ought to be reduced.
